A project setting chooses the close

planted projects with `close: scoped`, `close: strict` and no setting: a new project's config holds `close: scoped`; the scoped project runs the selection only, the strict project's close gives today's verdicts (every lifted gate still built); this repository's config reads `close: scoped`.
The scoped close runs only the selection

planted changes: to a shared-core file (its mapped suites selected, never the full suite), to the ticket's own file (its suite and the reachable suites), to record places or governance files alone (the record-reading suites named in the test map and nothing else, or nothing by themselves for governance files); a planted change with no mapping exits with the refusal and its reason and no widened set; the close's record shows no full-suite run.
One selection command for every level
`gov close --select <ticket>` on a planted ticket prints the scoped set and its `pytest` options, and the set equals the one a scoped close of the same ticket runs (compared in the close record).
Every failing test is run again alone

planted batches: a red the head without the batch also has with the same failure type is not the change's; a red the head does not have is the change's; a timeout or a failure with no record never matches (the change's); a load-sensitive case gets 3 rounds and others one each way; no clone is built for the nightly baseline (no such folder after the run); the nightly's recorded result is read first.
A red the change did not cause is named
a planted unowned red: the close record names it, a repair ticket for the orchestrator exists in `.tickets/`, and no accepted-reds or load-sensitive list was read or written (file times unchanged).
A batch's culprit is found

a planted batch of three candidates, one causing a red: the build without that candidate is green, only it goes back, the other two land on the same run; a planted red no single candidate explains, and a candidate that cannot be isolated, each refuse the batch; no landing happens before the culprit is found.
Each close writes its close record

a close of a planted ticket writes a record holding the commit closed, the runs and counts, the review's verdict, each red with its reason and the culprits sent back; a field missing from the record is a failed check.
The nightly rebuilds its worktree
a planted nightly run with `GOV_SECRETS_FULL_SCAN` unset in the caller's environment: the stores are rebuilt with it set to 1 before the run, and the nightly's record says the full secrets scan ran.
Measured, in docs/research/W2-115-smart-close.md

the document holds, for three recorded batches (one clean, one with a caused red, one with an unowned red), the verdict of `close_build.py` and of this close side by side, and the two verdicts are equal on all three.
The close's clean clone is a warm one
two planted closes in a row: the second reuses the first's clone (same folder, reset, stores kept); a planted clone that cannot be reset is replaced by a fresh one and the record says so.
READY is computed, not declared

planted probe records: a complete structured verdict per KPI line with only out-of-scope or non-ordinary findings gives READY; one in-scope, reachable, fails-open finding refuses; a malformed or incomplete verdict refuses; a verdict written by the ticket's lead over a reviewer's is refused.
`gov queue` gives W2-97

a planted queue of two batches, one green and one red with a culprit: the commit landed equals the commit tested (the same hash in both records), one run per batch on the merged result in a heavy-job slot, a run on identical merged code skipped with its reason, the red batch's culprit ejected and the rest advanced.
Each green run lands and closes in one step

a planted green run: the ticket's merge, its close record (run, counts, each red with its verdict, the baseline traced against) and its `closed` status all come from that run, the close cites the queue's record and runs no tests of its own; after the run no planted ticket is merged and not closed.
Nothing project-specific

grep of the close and queue code for this repository's branch names, paths and ticket ids finds 0 lines; a planted second repository's queue runs with the same code; this repository's queue runs on it and W2-97's tool is no longer called.
After each landing, the queue starts
a planted landing: the integration store's refresh (W2-116) is started once afterwards and the queue's own warm clones are seeded from that store, both visible in the queue's record.
When the integration branch moved during a run

planted moves: only record or governance files changed: the queue merges onto the new head and re-runs only the record-reading suites, then advances; any other file in the move: the whole selection re-runs; an unreadable record-reading set: the whole selection re-runs.
The queue keeps its work clones between runs

two planted runs: the second finds its clone reset to the head, untracked files removed, stores kept and the rebuild incremental; an unresettable clone is replaced by a fresh one; the record holds the rebuild's seconds per run, warm against fresh.
A scoped close refused by a red its change did not cause
a planted unowned red in a scoped close: the close does not refuse on it; a planted red the change caused: the close does not close.
A scoped close that runs the full suite

a scoped close of a planted ticket: the test runner's call list holds no full-suite run, and the accepted-reds and load-sensitive lists are neither opened nor written (file access or file times show none).
A batch that closes a culprit
a planted batch with one culprit, and one with a red no candidate explains: the culprit is not closed, and the unexplained batch closes nothing.
The strict close changed in any verdict
the strict-mode close run on the recorded planted cases from before the change: every verdict and every refusal is the same as the recorded one.
A branch advanced to a commit that was not the one tested
a planted queue run where the branch head moves after the test, and one where the run is red: the branch is not advanced in either; the advanced hash always equals the tested hash.
A second run on identical code
a planted queue with two batches whose merged code is identical: only one test run is recorded, and the skip carries its reason.
